newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Belarus leader worried by new Russia treaty draft.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader worried by new Russia treaty draft.

text.p: Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko expressed concern on Saturday about the latest draft of a charter on union with Russia and said Russian authorities were not yet ready to create a single state.
"Russia is not ready for a single state...I back (a single state), we are ready for this and I will prove this to the Russian people," Lukashenko told Russian television.
The latest draft, dated May 8, was "a step backwards" from previous documents, he said.
The Kremlin said earlier this week that a final version of the charter on union between the two Slav states should be ready for signing by the presidents of the two countries on May 23.
The charter will accompany an outline document signed by Lukashenko and Russian President Boris Yeltsin early last month.

The latest versions of the charter provide for a loose union with little practical power delegated to it and make clear that both Russia and Belarus will remain sovereign states. Many details remain vague.
Opinion polls in Russia and Belarus have shown a majority of people in both countries back the idea of closer integration and even merger.
Nationalists in Belarus and liberals in Russia both oppose the deal, fearing either a loss of independence or that it could provide a way for the authoritarian Lukashenko to secure greater powers.
Critics in Russia, Belarus and the West accuse Lukashenko of abuse of human rights in his country of 10 million people.
Lukashenko denied the charge. "Human rights are about the right to work, the right to receive your wages," he said, in a clear reference to a spiral of non-payments crippling the Russian economy.
"Our pensions are lower, but they are paid, like in Soviet days. Why have higher wages and higher pensions if you do not pay them."
